data.name: Hakima
data.gender_notes: Hakima is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: A woman of knowledge and wisdom, a scholar. Derived from the Arabic root h-k-m meaning 'to be wise' or 'to have knowledge'. In Islamic tradition, Hakima is a title of respect given to wise women. The name Hakima carries the meaning “Wise woman, Scholar” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Hakima usually hope their child will grow to embody wise woman, scholar and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Hakima belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Wise woman, Scholar.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hakima total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The title "Hakima" holds significant cultural importance as it is a title of respect and reverence, similar to Dr. or Professor in the western world. It is given to women who have acquired a high level of knowledge and wisdom, making them esteemed figures in their communities. This title, reflecting the Arabic roots of Islam, is prevalent in Islamic literature, including the tales of the renowned female heroines and scholars of the Islamic Golden Age.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual sense, a 'Hakima' embodies the Islamic virtues of knowledge, wisdom, and patience. As knowledge is a fundamental component of faith, the pursuit of wisdom is a lifelong endeavor for every Muslim. A 'Hakima' is an embodiment of this Islamic principle, demonstrating the value of knowledge and its role in one's personal growth and development. Being wise also means being able to provide counsel and make informed decisions, reflecting the spirit of compassion and the desire to help others. This title, thus, highlights the moral and spiritual aspect of Islamic living, encouraging individuals to strive for knowledge, wisdom, and understanding, not only for personal growth but also for the betterment of their communities.
